problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F=f+ψ over a convex measurable set Q; f is convex and continuously differentiable on E, and ψ is convex on Q. A minimizer exists.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: objective; spec.admissible convexity and minimizer clauses.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The objective combines a differentiable function f with a possibly nonsmooth convex term ψ, handled through an exact composite Bregman proximal oracle.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: Instance, objective, proxObjective; spec.admissible proximal minimization clause.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A gradient query at x∈Q returns a dual vector g(x,ξ), with E[g(x,ξ)]=df(x). Seeds are independent and identically distributed. Only gradient and proximal queries are available.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: Query; spec.admissible oracle and unbiasedness clauses. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: For a>0, z∈Q∩U and dual vector v, the oracle returns an exact minimizer over Q of a(v(u−z)+ψ(u))+D_h(u,z), lying in Q∩U. Gradient and proximal calls share one fixed total oracle budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: Query.prox, proxObjective; spec.admissible proximal clause. LongTails/Template.lean: Setup.numOracles, executeWithTrace, Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public L0>0 and L1≥0 satisfy ‖df(x)−df(y)‖≤(L0+L1 M)‖x−y‖ whenever ‖df‖≤M along the segment from x to y. No global Lipschitz gradient bound is assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: Public.L0, Public.L1; spec.valid and spec.admissible segment smoothness clause.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public σ≥0 and 1<α≤2 bound the central dual-norm moment: E‖g(x,ξ)−df(x)‖^α≤σ^α for every x∈Q. Finite variance is not required when α<2.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: Public.σ, Public.α; spec.valid and spec.admissible moment clauses.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: E has an arbitrary norm, with gradients in its continuous dual. The differentiable mirror function h satisfies D_h(u,z)≥‖u−z‖²/2 for z∈Q∩U and u∈Q; U is open and convex. No bounded domain or upper bound on Bregman divergence is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: Public, Dual, divergence; spec.admissible geometry clauses.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel measurable structure; no inner-product structure is required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All numerical parameters and x0 are public. A common minimizer x⋆ satisfies D_h(x⋆,x0)≤R²/2, F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ and ‖df(x⋆)‖≤G, with R,Δ>0 and G≥0. The functions, feasible set, mirror function and minimizer are hidden instance data.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: Public, Instance; spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible initialization clause.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable output x with F(x)−F(x⋆)≤ε, where ε>0 and x⋆ minimizes F over Q. No particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output must belong to Q on the success event.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: For public 0<δ<1, P{x∉Q or F(x)−F(x⋆)>ε}≤δ, over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedMirror.lean: spec.valid, spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence joint probability law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines gradient-dependent generalized smoothness, finite central α-moment noise, composite Bregman proximal geometry in an arbitrary finite-dimensional norm, and a high-probability feasible objective-gap guarantee.
